 No rain expected in the forecast for qathet on Halloween
 Haunted walks, pumpkin carving and many more fall activities take place this week/weekend 
 Tanya Hill 
 Oct 28, 2026 12:30 PM 
 Share by Email 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 Share on LinkedIn 
 Print 
 Share via Text Message 
 The weather forecast for Halloween day and night on Saturday, October 31, is expected to be calm and clear, with a mix of sun and cloud with a high of nine degrees. 
 Pavel Muraveu, iStock, Getty Images Plus 
 This week in qathet, fall weather has set in, temperatures are getting cooler and the rainy season has begun.
 Today, Wednesday, October 28, rain is expected later today, with a risk of a thunderstorm, a high of eight degrees and a low of plus four degrees overnight.
 For Thursday, October 29, cloudy skies are in the forecast with showers throughout the day, a high of six degrees and a low of plus one.
 No rain is in the forecast for Friday, October 30, and Saturday, October 31; a mix of sun and cloud is expected, with a high of nine degrees in the daytime, dropping to plus one degree overnight.
 The qathet region's event calendar is full of Halloween and fall activities this week:
 qathet Museum and Archives is hosting haunted walking tours beginning on Thursday, October 29, until Sunday, November 1. This one-hour guided tour explores local history and the ghosts said to linger in the neighbourhood of Townsite. Book online or in person at 4798 Marine Avenue.
 Also on October 29, an event called The Alley: Artist Card Trading Night takes place at 4478 Marine Avenue, at 5:30 pm. Event organizers say artist trading cards are self-made unique works or small series, signed and dated on the reverse by the artist/producer, exchanged and collected by the people who participate in this collaborative event. The event starts at 5:30 pm.
 On Friday, October 30, beginning at 4:30 pm, a pumpkin carving event is taking place at Powell River Recreation Complex (5001 Joyce Avenue).
 "Leave the mess with us and have your kids carve with us," stated event organizers.
 Pumpkins are included; register online or call 604.485.2891.
 Also on Friday, October 30, the ghost train is back at Paradise Valley Exhibition Park, from 6 until 8 pm. According to organizers, there will be family friendly train rides through the lights, with a bonfire and snacks provided by Just Frys and Dogs, plus more in the quonset.
On Friday and Saturday, a Spooky Halloween Forest Walk event will take place between 6 and 8 pm at Twin Eagles Bluff (1930 Twin Eagles Road).
 On Saturday, October 31, a Halloween gathering is happening at The Wishing Well art collective, called Do Not Come to this Party II: Resurrection, in Townsite (6251 Yew Street) beginning at 7 pm. 
 Also on Halloween night, Wildwood Public House (5987 Lund Street) will host a halloween party, with musicians Renelle and Dawson, followed by spooky music created by Count Christien.
 On Sunday, November 1, Texada Island Winter Market will take place at Texada Community Hall from 12 to 2 pm. There will be locally grown produce, soup and sandwiches available, baked goods, plus arts and crafts made by local artisans.
 Also on November 1, an event called Dia De Muertos Celebration – Parade and Community Ofrenda will take place. According to organizers, this annual event in qathet is inspired by the Mexican tradition of the Day of the Dead, where community members come together to collectively share their memories of loved ones who have left this world.
 "It is a vibrant celebration, with food, music, stories and beautiful altars to remember the dead," stated organizers. "Parade starts at the Wharf at Westview marina by totem pole at 2 pm; gathering at the Iguanas Mexican Grill 4312 Franklin Avenue afterwards."
